There are other terminals storing transportation fuels throughout New England that could present an opportunity to accommodate SAF and Jet A storage and blending. Terminals with space could consider adding truck offloading infrastructure to receive SAF produced nearby. The following terminal operators expressed a willingness to consider receipt, storage, and blending of locally produced SAF at their terminals: Global Partners, Inland Fuel Terminals, Shell, Sprague Energy, and Sunoco Logistics. Section 3 and Appendix C provide details on terminal tanks, capacity, and fuel receiving and offloading modes. Any terminal will require a capital investment for storing and blending SAF and Jet A. The investment amount will vary based on infrastructure availability and if different fuel receipt and off-loading modes are needed to accommodate the fuel. Terminals will need to assess space to accommodate the infrastructure necessary to accommodate SAF and blending activities.
